question: Q02 (Bas. 25.7): in all witnesses the note list passes from παρυπάτη μέσων to μέση with no name for the diatonic lichanos of the meson tetrachord. Is a name to be supplied, and in what wording: a λιχανὸς μέσων διάτονος, b μέση διάτονος, c μέσων διάτονος, d no supplement, e διάτονος μέσων (Xylander)?

prior_assessment.note: The transcription holds. I checked Hiller p. 206 (page image n227). The 15 names are προσλαμβανόμενος, ὑπάτη ὑπατῶν, παρυπάτη ὑπατῶν, ὑπάτη διάτονος, ὑπάτη μέσων, παρυπάτη μέσων, μέσων διάτονος, μέση, παραμέση, τρίτη διεζευγμένη, διεζευγμένη διάτονος, νήτη διεζευγμένη, τρίτη ὑπερβολαίων, διάτονος ὑπερβολαίων, νήτη ὑπερβολαίων. The brackets run from διὰ δ΄ ἐπίτριτος to δὶς διὰ πασῶν τετραπλάσιος. 'Decisive' is overstated, for four reasons. (1) Hiller calls the diagram 'neglegentissime facta' and does not say whose hand drew it. (2) Codex A is later than 1008: s. XI or XII according to Hiller and ARCA, s. XII according to Pinakes/Mioni. (3) The direction of dependence is unknown: the diagram could be the text's source, its sibling or its derivative. (4) It differs from the text at two places (παραμέση against παράμεσος; διεζευγμένη διάτονος against διάτονος διεζευγμένη). It is the best single piece of evidence for c, but it does not prove c.

Checked on the page image of Jan p. 264 (Nicomachus, Ench. 12, Meibom pp. 27-28). The list mixes the two orders: διάτονος ὑπατῶν, then μέσων διάτονος and συνημμένων διάτονος, then διάτονος διεζευγμένων and διάτονος ὑπερβολαίων. Jan's apparatus (p. 265) has '34 νήτη διεζ. om. R'.

Checked on the image of Jan p. 333.6-7: ἡ λιχανὸς τῶν μέσων ἤτοι διάτονος μέσων. The OCR of p. 332 has 'ἥτις καὶ διάτονος ὑπάτων ἐκαλεῖτο ἐν τῷ διατονικῷ γένει'. The claim that e is not the form of the text's model list is an inference, not a checked fact.

Cleonides, Jan p. 182 (image checked) and pp. 186-187 (OCR) have λιχανὸς ὑπάτων/μέσων διάτονος. The Alypius tables (OCR, Jan pp. 368-369) have ὑπάτων/μέσων διάτονος. The inference that this author never uses λιχανός is sound for this list.

The form διάτονος μέσων is real (Jan p. 333.7, checked). But it is not 'the standard name' even in Gaudentius: at c. 8, Jan p. 338.7 (checked), he writes ἀπὸ μέσων διατόνου ἐπὶ παραμέσην, and his sign lists (c. 23, p. 352, OCR) have Μέσων διάτονος.
Alypius' Lydian diatonic (Jan pp. 368-369, OCR) has ὑπάτων διάτονος, μέσων διάτονος, συνημμένων διάτονος, διεζευγμένων διάτονος, ὑπερβολαίων διάτονος, with παραμέση.
Same as Q02-04, checked on the image of Jan p. 182.

I saw only the sourcelibrary OCR of Wallis p. 89, not the page image. It has λιχανὸν ὑπατῶν and λιχανὸν μέσων by position and no note called διάτονος. Ptolemy does not bear on the wording. The argument against d rests better on the text's own next sentence (1st to 8th as 8th to 15th, in a fifteen-note system) and on Nicomachus, Jan p. 258 (mese is eighth of fifteen).
Checked on the image of Jan p. 182: λιχανὸς μέσων διάτονος stands between παρυπάτη μέσων and μέση. It attests the wording of a for Cleonides only.

Checked on the image of Jan p. 165: 'ὁ δὲ μβ ὑπερβολαίων διάτονος' (165.10) and 'μέσων διάτονον' (165.19); apparatus '19 μέσον MN'. Note that Euclid also has ὑπερβολαίων διάτονος with the genitive first, unlike this text.

Checked on the image of Jan p. 258. The text reads 'λιχανὸς μέσων, ὃν καὶ διάτονον καλοῦσιν' and 'εἶτα παράμεσος μετὰ ὅλον τόνον'; mese is ὀγδόη ἐν πεντεκαίδεκα φθόγγοις. Apparatus: '20 ἑξῆς δὲ — παρυπάτη μέσων om. R'.
I did not open the Strunk translation. Its substance is confirmed by the Greek of Cleonides (Jan p. 182).
OCR of Jan's apparatus to p. 183: '24 om. λιχανὸς ὑπάτων W', '28 μέση om. W'. Also p. 182 (image): '14 διάτονος, νήτη συν. om. W'. Omissions inside note lists are common.
OCR of Jan p. 257: 'διάτονος ὑπατῶν ἢ λιχανὸς ὑπατῶν. οὐδὲν γὰρ διαφέρει ὁποτερωσοῦν ὀνομάζειν'. It does not establish the word order of the meson name.
General lexicon entries; they do not discriminate between the options.

new_findings.source: E. Hiller, Theonis Smyrnaei Expositio (1878), p. 206 (diagram and note) and p. 72 apparatus; page images n227 and n93
new_findings.found: Hiller's note on p. 206: 'Exstat haec descriptio neglegentissime facta in cod. A post finem eius partis qua de musica agitur (p. 72). Quindecim nominibus adiecta sunt haec signa: ϙ ξ̄ R̄ Φ̄ C̄ P̄ u ιξ ζC εu U ϑq u Π K̄. Cf. Boeth. de inst. mus. p. 312 sqq.' His apparatus at p. 72.20 reads 'cf. descr. post finem libri'. So in A the diagram stands after 72.20, at the end of Theon's section on dividing the tone, just before περὶ δὲ τῆς ἐν ἀριθμοῖς ἁρμονίας. Hiller says nothing about the hand; he marks later corrections elsewhere as A². Name by name against the text, the diagram has the same 1-6 and 8 (μέση; the text has μέση μόνως). It shares the text's odd forms ὑπάτη διάτονος, τρίτη διεζευγμένη, νήτη διεζευγμένη and διάτονος ὑπερβολαίων. It differs at two places: παραμέση against the text's παράμεσος, and διεζευγμένη διάτονος against the text's διάτονος διεζευγμένη. In seventh place it has μέσων διάτονος.
new_findings.how: This is the closest parallel. A 15-name list shares four peculiar forms with the text, which shows the two are related, and its 7th name is μέσων διάτονος. Its weight is limited because it is later than 1008, its hand is unknown, and it may itself derive from the Quadrivium.

new_findings.source: Hiller, praefatio pp. V-VI (OCR of the scan); Pinakes diktyon 69778; ARCA manuscript 32720
new_findings.found: Codex A is Venice, Marc. gr. Z. 307 (coll. 1027). Hiller: parchment, 'saeculi XI. vel XII.', square format, contains only the first part of Theon (pp. 1-119); a second hand (A²) corrected it. Hiller holds that all other manuscripts of the complete first or second part descend from A or B; only an excerpt (pp. 46.20-51.6) came down by another route. Pinakes: s. XII, ff. 1-110v, Theon 'cum scholiis librarii et Bessarionis' (from Mioni, Codices graeci manuscripti II, 1985); Bessarion was its owner. ARCA (https://arca.irht.cnrs.fr/manuscript/32720) dates it s. XI-XII and has a 1975 IRHT microfilm, but the images are not freely viewable.
new_findings.how: Dates the diagram to after 1008 and probably after H (1040). So the diagram may depend on the Quadrivium, or both may go back to an older Theon exemplar. The direction cannot be settled from what is accessible.

new_findings.found: '20 προσλαμβανόμενος ὑπατὴ μέσων νητὴ διεζευγμένη mg. A'. A marginal note in A uses the nominative νήτη διεζευγμένη.
new_findings.how: The nominative διεζευγμένη, shared by the text and the diagram, also occurs in A's marginalia. This strengthens the link between the diagram and A's annotation layer.

new_findings.source: Theon (Thrasyllus' division of the canon), Hiller pp. 88.18, 91.12-13, 91.24, 92.2, 92.11-12 (images n109, n112, n113)
new_findings.found: Theon writes ἡ καὶ διάτονος ὑπατῶν (88.18); τὴν διάτονον τῶν ὑπερβολαίων (91.12-13); διάτονος καὶ νήτη συνημμένων (91.24); διάτονος συνημμένων (92.2); but τὴν τῶν μέσων διάτονον (92.11-12).
new_findings.how: The author's known source puts διάτονος first for the other tetrachords but the genitive first for the meson, the same split as this text's list.

new_findings.source: Nicomachus, Ench. 12, ed. Jan, MSG p. 264, apparatus p. 265 (images n365, n366)
new_findings.found: A mixed list: διάτονος ὑπατῶν; μέσων διάτονος; συνημμένων διάτονος; διάτονος διεζευγμένων; διάτονος ὑπερβολαίων. Apparatus: '15 ὑπ. μέση vid. M¹. 34 νήτη διεζ. om. R'.
new_findings.how: A typological parallel: in a list that otherwise puts διάτονος first for the diezeugmenon and hyperbolaion, the meson name has the genitive first. It also shows a single name dropping out of a note list (R).

new_findings.source: Nicomachus, Ench. 11, Jan p. 258 (image n359) and p. 257 (OCR)
new_findings.found: 'μετὰ δὲ τόνον λιχανὸς μέσων, ὃν καὶ διάτονον καλοῦσιν'; 'εἶτα παράμεσος'; ἡ μέση ... ἐν πεντεκαίδεκα φθόγγοις ὀγδόη. Apparatus: '20 ἑξῆς δὲ — παρυπάτη μέσων om. R'; '25 παραμέσος R'.
new_findings.how: Mese is eighth of fifteen, so a name is missing (against d). Nicomachus also uses παράμεσος, as the text does.

new_findings.source: Gaudentius, Isagoge 6 and 8, Jan p. 333.6-7 and p. 338.6-7 (images n434, n439); c. 23, p. 352 (OCR)
new_findings.found: c. 6: 'ἡ λιχανὸς τῶν μέσων ἤτοι διάτονος μέσων'. c. 8: 'ἐπὶ δύο τόνων ἀπὸ μέσων διατόνου ἐπὶ παραμέσην'. c. 23 (Hypolydian sign list): Ὑπάτων διάτονος, Μέσων διάτονος, Παράμεσος, Διεζευγμένων διάτονος.
new_findings.how: The same author uses both διάτονος μέσων (e) and μέσων διάτονος (c).

new_findings.source: Alypius, Lydian diatonic, Jan pp. 368-369 (OCR of the scan)
new_findings.found: Names: ὑπάτων διάτονος, μέσων διάτονος, συνημμένων διάτονος, διεζευγμένων διάτονος, ὑπερβολαίων διάτονος. First (vocal) signs: Φ for ὑπάτων διάτονος; C for ὑπάτη μέσων; Ρ for παρυπάτη μέσων; Μ for μέσων διάτονος; Ι for μέση; Ζ for παραμέση; Ε for τρίτη διεζευγμένων; ⊔ (ὦ τετράγωνον ὕπτιον) for διεζευγμένων διάτονος; υ for τρίτη ὑπερβολαίων. My comparison: the signs Hiller prints for the diagram (positions 4-11 and 13: Φ, C, P, u ≈ μ, ι, ζ, ε, U, u) match this Lydian vocal series.
new_findings.how: The diagram's 7th name comes with the sign of μέσων διάτονος, so the diagram was built on a Lydian notation table whose name is μέσων διάτονος. This explains its 7th name. It also leaves open that a later diagram-maker filled the gap from such a table rather than from the author.

new_findings.source: Boethius, De institutione musica IV.3 (Friedlein pp. 310-312) and I.22 (pp. 214-215); OCR of the scan
new_findings.found: IV.3 (Lydian notation; the passage Hiller cites): hypaton diatonos, meson diatonos, synemmenon diatonos, diezeugmenon diatonos, hyperboleon diatonos, paramesos. I.22: 'lichanos meson, simpliciter in diatono quidem genere diatonos meson', diatonos synemmenon, diatonos diezeugmenon, diatonos hyperboleon.
new_findings.how: Latin evidence for both orders: c in the notational tradition, e in the Nicomachean descriptive tradition. Xylander's e may reflect the latter, or the list's own διάτονος-first forms.

new_findings.source: Euclid, Sectio canonis 20, Jan p. 165 (image n266)
new_findings.found: 'ὁ δὲ μβ ὑπερβολαίων διάτονος' (165.10) and 'μέσων διάτονον' (165.19); apparatus '19 μέσον MN'.

new_findings.source: Excerpta ex Nicomacho 9 (Jan pp. 280-281) and Bacchius 13 (Jan p. 295); OCR of the scan
new_findings.found: Excerpta: ὑπατῶν διάτονος, μέσων διάτονος, συνημμένων διάτονος, διεζευγμένων διάτονος, ὑπερβολαίων διάτονος, with παράμεσος. Bacchius: [ὑπατῶν διάτονον], [μέσων διάτονον], [συνημμένων διάτονον]; Jan notes 'sonorum nomina solus habet M'.

new_findings.source: Anonymus Bellermanni §§69-70, ed. F. Bellermann (1841), p. 79 (page image n98)
new_findings.found: §69: 'διάτονοι πέντε· ὑπατῶν διάτονος, μέσων διάτονος, συνημμένων διάτονος, διεζευγμένων διάτονος, ὑπερβολαίων διάτονος· μέση μία· παράμεσος μία'. §70: 'ἀπὸ παρυπάτης μέσων ἐπὶ μέσων διάτονον τόνος· ἀπὸ μέσων διατόνου ἐπὶ μέσην τόνος'. Apparatus: '69. μέσων διάτονος, συνημμένων διάτονος om. p. — ὑπερβολαίων διάτονος om. P'; '70 ... verba ἡμιτόνιον· ἀπὸ τρίτης διεζευγμένων ἐπὶ διεζευγμένων διάτονον solus N. servavit'.
new_findings.how: μέσων διάτονος in the position between παρυπάτη μέσων and μέση. The name μέσων διάτονος itself dropped out of a note list in one manuscript (p), and the editor restored it from the others: the editorial practice this question needs.

new_findings.source: Aristides Quintilianus I.6, Meibom, Antiquae musicae auctores septem (1652), vol. II, p. 9 (page image n532)
new_findings.found: ὑπατῶν διάτονος, ὑπάτη μέσων, παρυπάτη μέσων, μέσων ἐναρμόνιος, μέσων χρωματική, μέσων διάτονος, μέση ... παράμεσος, τρίτη διεζευγμένων.

new_findings.source: Cleonides, Isagoge 4, Jan p. 182 (image n283) and pp. 184-187 (OCR)
new_findings.found: λιχανὸς μέσων διάτονος stands between παρυπάτη μέσων and μέση. Apparatus: '14 διάτονος, νήτη συν. om. W'; '21 22 νήτη et παρανήτη invertit W'. At pp. 186-187 Jan notes eye-skips: 'aberraverunt enim M¹W ad lin. 22'.
new_findings.how: Attests the wording of a, but only in the λιχανός/παρανήτη terminology that this list never uses. It also shows omissions and inversions of names in transmitted note lists.

new_findings.source: Searches for the form μέση διάτονος: OCR texts of Jan's MSG, Hiller's Theon, Bellermann's Anonymus, Meibom/AQ, Friedlein's Boethius ('mese diatonos'), and a web search
new_findings.found: No occurrence of μέση διάτονος (or μέσης διατόνου) as a note name anywhere. Every source treats μέση as a fixed note (Alypius ch. 4, Jan p. 368: ἑστῶτες ... μέση).
new_findings.how: Against b: unattested, and it would make a fixed note a diatonic variant.

searched_without_result:
1. A modern codicological description of the diagram in Marc. gr. Z. 307: its folio, its hand (first hand, A² or later), and whether it was copied from A's exemplar. Mioni's 1985 catalogue is not online. ARCA has a 1975 IRHT microfilm, but its images are not freely viewable (no viewer on the page). Searches for studies of the diagram (Petrucci 2012, Delattre Biencourt 2010, Brodersen 2021) found nothing accessible.
2. J. Dupuis, Théon de Smyrne (1892), checked through the archive.org OCR (thenossmyrnaioup00theo). His preface (p. IX) only repeats Hiller's dating of A. At the corresponding place (his §§16-17, pp. 116-117) he neither reproduces nor discusses the diagram.
3. ὑπάτη διάτονος outside the Theon-A diagram: none in Jan's MSG, Bellermann's Anonymus or AQ, and the web search found nothing relevant.
4. μέση διάτονος: no attestation anywhere (see findings).
5. An independent source before 1008 that has the same 15-name list: none found.
6. Ptolemy, Harm. 2.5: Düring's edition is on archive.org only as an upload from an illegitimate source (Z-Library), so I did not use it. I saw only the sourcelibrary OCR of Wallis p. 89.
7. I also viewed an archive.org upload of Winnington-Ingram's 1963 Teubner AQ. Its licensing is unclear, so I do not rely on it. I took the AQ text from Meibom 1652 instead. The upload's apparatus reports R writing -νη for -νων in συνημμένων/διεζευγμένων, a parallel to the nominative τρίτη/νήτη διεζευγμένη; treat this as unverified.
decisive: Nothing is decisive. The closest parallel, the 15-name diagram in Theon's codex A (Hiller p. 206), shares four peculiar forms with this list and reads μέσων διάτονος in 7th place. But codex A was written after 1008 (s. XI-XII or s. XII), the diagram's hand is not reported, and the direction of dependence is unknown. It also differs from the text in two names, so the author did not copy it verbatim. Option e (διάτονος μέσων) is a genuine ancient form (Gaudentius 6; Boethius I.22), and it matches the διάτονος-first forms that sit next to it in this list.
reasoning:
Against d: the text's own next sentence (evidence file: Bas. 25.11-17; H 65r.2-8) describes a fifteen-note system in which the 1st note stands to the 8th as the 8th to the 15th. So μέση must be 8th, but in the transmitted list of 14 names it is 7th. Nicomachus (Jan p. 258: mese is eighth of fifteen) and the diagram's octave bracket, which ends at μέση, agree. A name has fallen out.

On the wording:

1. Option a, λιχανὸς μέσων διάτονος, is the Cleonidean name (Jan p. 182). This list, however, never uses λιχανός or παρανήτη, and names the movable diatonic notes with διάτονος alone. a goes against the author's usage.

2. Option b, μέση διάτονος, is unattested anywhere I could search. It would make the fixed mese look like a diatonic variant. Its one attraction is internal. On the pattern of ὑπάτη διάτονος, 'μέση διάτονος, μέση μόνως' would explain μόνως and offer a clean eye-skip (μέση…μέση). But μόνως is just as well explained after any meson-named note: the three preceding notes all carry μέσων, and then comes μέση 'simply'. Also, the diagram, which shares ὑπάτη διάτονος, has the genitive μέσων here.

3. Between c and e: e (διάτονος μέσων) is attested (Gaudentius 6; Boethius I.22) and agrees with the neighbouring διάτονος διεζευγμένη and διάτονος ὑπερβολαίων. It also gives a textbook homoeoteleuton: παρυπάτη μέσων· [διάτονος μέσων·] μέση. Five things favour c:
   - c is by far the commoner form: Euclid, Excerpta Nicomachi, Alypius, Bacchius (M), Gaudentius 8 and 23, AQ, Anon. Bell., Boethius IV.3.
   - In the lists that mix the two orders, the meson name has the genitive first while the others have διάτονος first. This is the case in Nicomachus Ench. 12 (διάτονος ὑπατῶν, μέσων διάτονος, διάτονος διεζευγμένων, διάτονος ὑπερβολαίων) and in Theon, the author's known source (διάτονος ὑπατῶν, διάτονον τῶν ὑπερβολαίων, διάτονος συνημμένων, but τὴν τῶν μέσων διάτονον). That is exactly the profile this list would have with c.
   - The diagram related to this list reads μέσων διάτονος. Its notation signs, which follow the Lydian diatonic series of Alypius and Boethius IV.3, put the sign for μέσων διάτονος (M, Hiller's 'u') in 7th place.
   - The loss of μέσων διάτονος is also easy to explain: homoeoarcton μέσων/μέση. Omissions of single names are common in transmitted note lists (Nicomachus R; Cleonides W). The Bellermann Anonymus' codex p omits precisely μέσων διάτονος.
   - Xylander's e has no witness behind it.

The evidence is moderate because the diagram's independence from this text, and its date relative to the archetype, cannot be established. If the diagram derives from a defective copy of the Quadrivium and was completed from an Alypian table, it shows only how a Byzantine reader filled the gap, not what the author wrote. In any case the apparatus should report the diagram (Theon cod. Marc. gr. Z. 307, Hiller p. 206, μέσων διάτονος), Xylander's διάτονος μέσων, and the 15-name requirement.
seen_prohibited:
1. Jan, MSG p. 338 (Gaudentius), commentary footnote 3: 'eadem docet Psellus mus. p. 28: συμφωνεῖ δὲ ἡ μὲν διὰ τεσσάρων διάστασις ...'. 'Psellus mus. p. 28' is evidently this text (Xylander's Basel page). I saw it on the page image and did not use it; it does not concern Q02.
2. Excluded writers turned up in apparatus notes: Jan p. 257, 'hinc usque ad p. 264,5 adhibendus erat Pachymeris liber'; Jan pp. 182 and 258 mention Pachymeres and Bryennius; Hiller's praefatio mentions Bryennius' Theon excerpt; the AQ apparatus mentions Bry. I did not use any of them.
3. I did not open any edition, transcription or translation of this text, and I put no Greek phrase of it into a search engine. The only Greek web searches were for the note-name terms 'μέση διάτονος' and 'ὑπάτη διάτονος'; neither returned a hit on this text.
